lead: Augusta is still rebuilding from Hurricane Helene, which tore through the city in 2024. Fallen trees, roof leaks and long power outages left damage in nearly every neighborhood.
risk: hurricane and tree damage, roof leaks and mobile home leaks
risk_short: hurricane and tree damage, roof leaks
why: Hurricane Helene reached Augusta in the early hours of September 27, 2024, still packing strong winds after crossing Georgia. Huge oaks and pines came down on houses, cars and power lines across the city. Some homes were without power for well over a week. Each fallen tree can open a roof to rain, and ceilings, walls and floors soaked through in the storms that followed.

Augusta also has a large share of mobile and manufactured homes, close to 6% of all housing. Leaks under these homes can rot the floor before anyone sees water. About half of Augusta homes were built before 1980, so old drains and supply lines add risk. Low areas near the Savannah River and its creeks can flood when heavy rain stalls over the city.
image_alt: Damaged house with a broken roof and exposed interior
image_caption: Helene's winds brought down trees across Augusta, opening roofs to rain.
problems: Wooded areas like Summerville, Forest Hills
Low areas near the river and creeks
tips: Have a tree service check large trees near the house.
Tarp a damaged roof fast to stop more rain from getting in.
Check under a mobile home for drips and soft spots twice a year.
Take photos of every room before storm season for your claim.
areas: Calls come from Summerville, Harrisburg, Olde Town, Pinch Gut, National Hills, Forest Hills, West Augusta and Laney-Walker, plus Hephzibah, Martinez and Evans.

faq.q: Does insurance cover a tree that fell on my Augusta house?
faq.a: Most home policies cover damage when a tree falls on the house, plus removal up to a set limit. Water that gets in through the hole is usually covered too if you act fast to stop it. Take photos, tarp the roof and call your insurer as soon as you can.
